properties.title: Flood Advisory issued November 9 at 2:43AM CST until November 9 at 8:00AM CST by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Kinney County in south central Texas...
Northeastern Maverick County in south central Texas...
Southwestern Uvalde County in south central Texas...
Northwestern Zavala County in south central Texas...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM CST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 243 AM CST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1.5 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Eagle Pass, Uvalde, El Indio, Chula Vista, Dabney, Blewett,
Paloma, Washer, Cline, Uvalde Estates, Rosita, Elm Creek, Siesta
Acres, Fabrica, Seco Mines, Las Quintas Fronterizas and Eidson
Road.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.
properties.area: Kinney, TX; Maverick, TX; Uvalde, TX; Zavala, TX

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued November 9 at 1:04AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Los Olmos Creek Near Falfurrias affecting Brooks County.

.Excessive rainfall is forecast to continue upstream of Los Olmos
into early this week, leading to a rise in river levels that may
approach action stage late tonight.

For the Los Olmos Creek...including Falfurrias...elevated river
levels are forecast.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Los Olmos Creek near Falfurrias.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding reaches 120 feet wide
into flood plain-persons vulnerable to lowland flooding should move
equipment to higher ground.

At 9.0 feet, Flow is high enough to close FM 1418 as water is
covering the bridge.

At 10.0 feet, Flow escapes from the Los Olmos drainage into the Palo
Blanco drainage area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:15 AM CST Monday the stage was 1.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 10.0 feet
tomorrow morning.
- Action stage is 5.0 feet. The river is expected to reach action
stage late tonight.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you are in the advisory area, remain alert to possible flooding or
the possibility of the advisory being upgraded to a warning.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 115 PM CST.
